answer:
### 1. Execution Environment: Local vs. Hosted API

The `fast-jev-compaction` classifier does **not** run as a local model on your machine [1, 2]. Instead, it makes HTTPS calls to a hosted System 1 decision API operated by TypeSafe at `https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone` [2, 3]. 

To use the plugin, users must provide a `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, which authenticates requests sent to TypeSafe's hosted servers in the United States [2, 3]. While local System 1 decision models (such as Laia/Jebadiah 27B) exist in broader Jev architectural implementations, the `fast-jev-compaction` plugin specifically targets the remote `api.typesafe.ai` endpoint [2, 4, 5].

---

### 2. Conversation Data Transmitted Off the Machine

When compaction triggers, `fast-jev-compaction` constructs a payload and sends the following off your local machine to TypeSafe's US servers [2, 6]:

* **Transmitted Content**:
  * The **full conversation transcript** (all user prompts and assistant text, in chronological order, truncated only if exceeding the state token ceiling) [6].
  * **Tool inputs** up to 1,000 characters per call, which includes exact CLI commands, file paths, and code snippets contained within edit commands [2, 6].
  * The user's **3 most recent messages**, which serve as the task intent context for Jev [6].

* **Omitted Content**:
  * The **raw content of tool outputs (`tool_result`)** is **not** transmitted [2]. Tool results are stripped out and replaced with a brief metadata note stating their length (e.g., `ok, 4213 chars (omitted)`) [2].

* **Privacy & Security Risks**:
  * Any **sensitive credentials, API keys, personal client data, or proprietary code** included in user prompts or tool inputs (such as inline secrets in shell commands or edited code blocks) are sent directly to TypeSafe's servers [2, 7, 8].
  * TypeSafe's privacy policy states that data is retained for as long as reasonably necessary to provide the service, with no option for zero data retention [2].
  * Credentials embedded in shell commands are not automatically redacted prior to transmission [7].

---

### 3. Installation & Integration in Claude Code

`fast-jev-compaction` is a community plugin created by Tamara Tran [1, 9]. It is installed as a Claude Code mod via the GitHub marketplace [9]:

1. **Marketplace Addition & Installation**:
   ```bash
   claude plugin marketplace add tamaratran/fast-jev-compaction
   claude plugin install fast-jev-compaction@fast-jev-compaction
   ```
   Alternatively, these commands can be run inside an active session using `/plugin` [9].

2. **Configuration & Parameters**:
   The plugin is configured using `/plugin configure fast-jev-compaction@fast-jev-compaction` or by editing `pluginConfigs` in `~/.claude/settings.json` [10-12]. Key configuration parameters include [10, 12, 13]:
   * `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`: Stored in OS credential storage or environment variables [10, 12].
   * `compactAtPercent`: Threshold percentage of the total context window (e.g., `25` for a 1M token window) that triggers auto-compaction [10, 14].
   * `keepThreshold`: Probability cutoff score (default `0.5`, recommended `0.2`) [10, 15].

3. **Execution Hook**:
   The mod hooks directly into Claude Code's compaction events [14, 16]. When triggered automatically by `compactAtPercent` or manually via the `/compact` command, the plugin intercepts the event, scores the history via Jev, and replaces generative summarization with verbatim tool pruning [14, 16, 17].

---

### 4. Pruning Logic: Keep, Truncate, and Drop

Unlike native Claude Code compaction—which replaces conversation history with an LLM-generated summary—`fast-jev-compaction` performs **verbatim pruning** without paraphrasing any text [1, 18, 19].

```
                     ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
                     │          Compaction Triggered           │
                     └────────────────────┬────────────────────┘
                                          │
                  ┌───────────────────────┴───────────────────────┐
                  ▼                                               ▼
     ┌─────────────────────────┐                     ┌─────────────────────────┐
     │  Pinned & User/AI Text  │                     │   Historical Tool Calls │
     │  (1st msg, 6 recent)    │                     │   & Tool Results        │
     └────────────┬────────────┘                     └────────────┬────────────┘
                  │                                               │
                  ▼                                               ▼
         Keep 100% Verbatim                               Score via Jev
                                                                  │
                   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                   ▼                                              ▼                                              ▼
     [ Both Call & Result Pass ]                   [ Only Tool Call Passes ]                      [ Both Below Cutoff ]
                   │                                              │                                              │
                   ▼                                              ▼                                              ▼
         KEEP: Retain 100%                             TRUNCATE: Keep call,                          DROP: Remove both
         verbatim tool call                             truncate output to                            call & result
         & full output [15]                            head chars (e.g., 300) [15]                  completely [15]
```

* **Pinned Messages**:
  * The **first message** of the transcript and the **6 most recent messages** (`preserveRecentMessages`) are pinned and never modified or dropped [13, 15, 17].
* **Text Messages**:
  * All user prompts and assistant textual responses are retained **100% verbatim** in their original order [1, 17, 19].
* **Historical Tool Call / Result Pairs**:
  For all tool pairs outside the pinned set, Jev evaluates two probability questions in a single parallel call [15, 17]:
  1. **Keep**: If both the tool call and tool result pass `keepThreshold`, the call and its entire output are kept 100% verbatim [15].
  2. **Truncate**: If only the tool call passes `keepThreshold`, the tool call (command or path) is retained, but the output is truncated to its initial head characters (`truncatedToolResultHead`, default 300 chars) plus a truncation note [13, 15, 17].
  3. **Drop**: If both the tool call and output fall below `keepThreshold`, both the tool call and its output are completely dropped [15].

---

### 5. Benchmark Measurement (~1M to ~86k Tokens) & Task-Outcome Validation

* **How It Was Measured**:
  * The widely cited result—reducing a session of nearly **1,000,000 tokens down to ~86,000 tokens**—was measured and reported on X (formerly Twitter) by Alex Volkov on a live, highly tool-heavy session [20].
  * The compaction executed in **~1 second** (with Jev API decision latencies measuring between 211ms and 743ms across benchmark runs), costing roughly \$0.004 to \$0.02 in TypeSafe API fees [16, 19-21].

* **Task-Outcome Validation & Known Issues**:
  * **Over-pruning Under Default Settings**: Benchmark evaluations in repository Issues 26 and 56 showed that with the default `keepThreshold: 0.5`, **88.8% to 96.4% of context text was removed**, and **zero tool calls were kept** across three measured test sessions [15].
  * **Task Degradation & Hallucinations**: In a recorded 22-minute test run (Issue 65), after the default pruning removed the tool calls that proved execution, Claude began hallucinating progress and reporting work it had not actually performed [15].
  * **Recommended Threshold**: To prevent task failure, measurements indicate setting `keepThreshold` to **`0.2`** (valid range `0.10` to `0.25`), which retains tool call records and partial outputs [10, 15].
  * **Fallback Mechanism**: The plugin enforces a `minReductionRatio` (default 0.25) [13, 17]. If Jev pruning yields less than a 25% token reduction, `fast-jev-compaction` aborts and falls back to Claude Code’s native generative summarizer [13, 17].
  * **Survival Test Verification**: To verify task outcome integrity post-compaction, users are advised to run a "Survival Test" prompt asking the agent to recall exact error messages, file paths, and active constraints [22].

---

### 6. Known Failure Modes

1. **Information Loss & Hallucinations (Issues 56 & 65)**:
   Because Jev uses probabilistic binary pruning, setting the threshold too high (`0.5`) deletes tool execution evidence [15]. This can lead to agents hallucinating completed work or losing track of active bugs [15].

2. **Context Re-inflation on Session Resume (`--resume` / Issue 89)**:
   When re-opening a compacted session using `claude --resume`, the pruned context is not properly persisted across reloads [22-24]. The session re-inflates to **~166,000–168,000 tokens**, compared to ~28,000 tokens for a session compacted via native summary [22, 23].

3. **Compaction Degradation Across Sequential Rounds (Issue 70)**:
   Since `fast-jev-compaction` only prunes tool calls and never compresses conversational text, repeated compactions accumulate unprunable text [23]. Eventually, the reduction ratio drops below 25%, causing the plugin to repeatedly fail and hand control back to native summarization [23].

4. **WAF / Firewall Blocks (HTTP 403 / Issue 97)**:
   TypeSafe's API firewall (Cloudflare) sometimes flags transcript snippets containing certain shell commands, SQL statements, or system paths, returning an HTML 403 error and forcing a fallback to native summarization [25, 26].

5. **Data Exposure & Unrequested Background Pings (Issue 107, PRs 64 & 98)**:
   Plaintext prompts, edited code, and shell commands are transmitted to third-party US servers without client-side credential scrubbing [2, 6, 7]. Additionally, sub-agents or pre-calculated compactions can trigger automatic background requests to Jev without explicit user initiation [7].

6. **Desktop GUI & Non-Terminal Incompatibility (PR 125)**:
   In Claude Code Desktop GUI or VS Code environments, percentage-based autocompact triggers fail to fire automatically, and UI feedback lines are not rendered [14, 24].

7. **API Provider Incompatibility (Issue 114)**:
   The plugin exclusively supports direct TypeSafe API keys (`api.typesafe.ai`) [5, 26]. Attempting to use OpenRouter or third-party proxy keys results in `401 Unauthorized` errors [5, 26].

---

💡 **Next Step**: Would you like me to share the recommended `CLAUDE.md` rules and `SessionStart` hook configuration to automatically protect your critical session notes from being lost during compaction?

Compactação Cirúrgica e Imunidade ao Context Decay À medida que uma sessão de codificação se aproxima do teto da janela de contexto ( ou de tokens), a atenção do modelo degrada-se progressivamente ( Context Decay ) 19 . A compactação nativa baseada em sumarização generativa (compact_20260112) leva de a , consome cerca de tokens de processamento e substitui o histórico técnico por uma paráfrase com perda de informação — retendo comandos exatos nos benchmarks comparativos 19 . A arquitetura substitui a sumarização por uma combinação de Compactação Verbatim Guiada pelo Jev (fast-jev-compaction) e Sobrevivência Determinística em Disco 3 . Em cada evento turn.complete, o harness verifica o tamanho do contexto em código e envia quatro perguntas em uma única chamada ao Jev: se a solicitação mudou de direção ( switched gears ), se o último turno concluiu uma unidade de trabalho, quanto do trabalho anterior o próximo passo necessita e se o agente está no meio de uma edição multi-etapas 3 . Quando a compactação é acionada, o plugin fast-jev-compaction (desenvolvido por Tamara Tran para Claude Code e portado para o Pi Agent como fast-jev-compaction-pi) fixa a primeira mensagem da transcrição e as mensagens mais recentes (preserveRecentMessages) e pontua todos os pares históricos de tool_call/tool_result em uma única requisição paralela ao Jev em a 19 . Para cada par, o Jev decide entre manter (keepThreshold: 0.5), truncar (truncateHeadChars: 300, retendo os primeiros caracteres antes da nota de corte) ou remover 19 . Tudo o que é mantido permanece 100% verbatim sem qualquer reescrita, reduzindo sessões de quase de tokens para tokens em um segundo e preservando comandos exatos e caminhos de arquivos no perfil ajustado ( fast-jev tuned ), com fallback seguro para o sumarizador nativo caso a redução de caracteres seja inferior a minReductionRatio: 0.25 19 .

Instrucao que voce deu so no chat pode sumir.

2. O que o corte do Jev faz Nunca resume. Todo texto teu e do Claude fica, palavra por palavra e na ordem, e so chamada e saida de ferramenta podem sair. A primeira mensagem e as 6 mais recentes nunca sao tocadas. 3. 4. Custo de uma compactacao no Jev Cada pedido leva no maximo 30 mil tokens, e com a conversa enviada no teto de 25 mil cabem umas 40 chamadas por pedido. Pela conta com o codigo do plugin e o preco de US$ 0,042 por milhao: 100 chamadas dao ate 3 pedidos, uns US$ 0,004, e 600 chamadas dao ate 15 pedidos, uns US$ 0,02. 5. Custo do resumo nativo O resumo e um pedido ao teu proprio modelo com a conversa inteira. No Opus 5.5 pela API, so ler 950 mil tokens do cache custa US$ 0,19, e com o cache frio custa US$ 3,80, antes de pagar a escrita do resumo a US$ 20 por milhao. No plano Pro ou Max nao tem fatura por pedido, mas sai do limite de uso.

9. Faca o teste de sobrevivencia A compactacao so serviu se o Claude ainda tem o que voce vai precisar daqui a vinte minutos. Logo depois do primeiro corte, cole o prompt Teste de sobrevivencia, que esta mais abaixo, e compare a resposta com o que voce sabe que aconteceu na sessao. Rode /context antes e depois pra ver quantos tokens sairam.  1) Mensagem de erro, caminho e restricao voltaram exatos: o corte esta bom. 2) Voltaram parafraseados ou com NAO TENHO: aquilo estava numa saida que foi cortada. Peca pra ele rodar a ferramenta de novo antes de seguir e considere descer o corte.  3) Ele afirma que fez algo e nao mostra comando nem arquivo: peca a prova, rodando de novo.
